ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the graph of the function f is a horizontal line between t=0 and t=1, and the function value is 2; from t=1 to t=2 it is a descending line segment, from the point (1,2) to the point (2,0), and this part is above the t-axis. Reasoning: By definition, G(x)=∫_0^x f(t)dt, H(x)=∫_2^x f(t)dt. Split the integration interval of G(x): G(x)=∫_0^2 f(t)dt+∫_2^x f(t)dt. The signed area from 0 to 2 on the graph is: the area of the rectangle from 0 to 1 is 2·1=2, plus the area of the triangle from 1 to 2 is (1·2)/2=1, so ∫_0^2 f(t)dt=3. Also because ∫_2^x f(t)dt=H(x), therefore G(x)=3+H(x).

method.method_draft: Use the text definitions to note that both G and H are accumulation functions for the same integrand f, so G'(x)=f(x) and H'(x)=f(x).
